summary: Someone whose close relative just died and is not yet buried is too busy to say Shema, daven, or put on tefillin. The people carrying the coffin also don't say Shema if they are needed.

chunks.en: Someone whose dead relative is lying in front of him, not yet buried,
chunks.st: One whose deceased relative is laid out unburied before him

chunks.en: does not have to say Shema,
chunks.st: is exempt from the recitation of Shema,

chunks.en: or daven Shemoneh Esrei, or put on tefillin.
chunks.st: from the Amida prayer, and from the mitzva to don phylacteries, until the deceased has been buried.

words.note: The main prayer we say standing, also called the Amidah.

chunks.en: The people who carry the coffin, the ones who take their place, and the ones who take their place after that,
chunks.st: With regard to the pallbearers and their replacements and the replacements of their replacements,

words.note: The bed or stretcher the person who died is carried on.

chunks.he: אֶת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה וְאֶת שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַמִּטָּה,
chunks.en: both those walking in front of the coffin and those behind it,
chunks.st: those located before the bier who have not yet carried the deceased and those located after the bier.

chunks.en: the ones who are needed to carry it do not have to say Shema,
chunks.st: Those who are needed to carry the bier are exempt from reciting Shema;

chunks.he: וְאֶת שֶׁאֵין לַמִּטָּה צֹרֶךְ בָּהֶן חַיָּבִין.
chunks.en: but the ones who are not needed to carry it must say Shema.
chunks.st: while those who are not needed to carry the bier, are obligated to recite Shema.

chunks.en: Both groups do not have to daven Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: However, both these and those are exempt from reciting the Amida prayer,
chunks.stMore: since they are preoccupied and are unable to focus and pray with the appropriate intent.

summary: After a funeral, people may start Shema only if they can finish before they reach the rows of people comforting the mourners. In those rows, only the people in the inside row are free from saying Shema.

chunks.en: If they buried the person who died and came back,
chunks.st: After they buried the deceased and returned,

chunks.en: if they can start and finish saying Shema
chunks.st: if they have sufficient time to begin to recite Shema and conclude
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz: finish all of Shema. Bartenura: finish just one section of it.

chunks.en: before they get to the rows of people,
chunks.st: before they arrive at the row,
chunks.stMore: formed by those who attended the burial, through which the bereaved family will pass in order to receive consolation,

words.note: After a burial, people stand in rows so the mourners can walk between them and be comforted.

chunks.en: they should start.
chunks.st: they should begin.

chunks.en: But if not, they should not start.
chunks.st: If they do not have sufficient time to conclude reciting the entire Shema, then they should not begin.

chunks.en: Of the people standing in the rows,
chunks.st: And those standing in the row,

chunks.en: the ones in the inside row do not have to say Shema,
chunks.st: those in the interior row, directly before whom the mourners will pass and who will console them, are exempt from reciting Shema,

words.note: The ones right next to the mourners, who comfort them.

chunks.en: but the ones in the outside row must say it.
chunks.st: while those in the exterior row, who stand there only to show their respect, are obligated to recite Shema.

summary: Women, slaves, and children don't have to say Shema or wear tefillin. But they do have to daven, have a mezuzah, and bentch after eating.

chunks.en: Women, slaves, and children do not have to
chunks.st: Women, slaves and minors are exempt

words.note: Servants who belonged to a Jewish master and kept some mitzvos.

chunks.en: say Shema or put on tefillin,
chunks.st: from the recitation of Shema and from phylacteries,

chunks.en: but they must daven and have a mezuzah,
chunks.st: but are obligated in prayer, mezuza

chunks.en: and bentch, the bracha after eating.
chunks.st: and Grace after Meals.

words.note: Bentching, the bracha said after eating bread.

summary: A man who is tamei from a certain kind of impurity may only think the Shema in his heart without saying the brachos. After food he says the bracha, but not before it. Rabbi Yehuda says he says the brachos before and after.
stIntro: Ezra the Scribe decreed that one who is ritually impure because of a seminal emission may not engage in matters of Torah until he has immersed in a ritual bath and purified himself. This halakha was accepted over the course of many generations; however, many disputes arose with regard to the Torah matters to which it applies. Regarding this, the mishna says:

chunks.he: בַּעַל קֶרִי מְהַרְהֵר בְּלִבּוֹ וְאֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ,
chunks.en: A man who is tamei in a certain way thinks the Shema in his heart and does not say the brachos,
chunks.st: If the time for the recitation of Shema arrived and one is impure due to a seminal emission, he may contemplate Shema in his heart, but neither recites the blessings

words.note: A kind of impurity from the body; he must go to the mikvah before learning Torah.

chunks.en: not before it and not after it.
chunks.st: preceding Shema, nor the blessings following it.

chunks.en: And for food, he says the bracha after eating,
chunks.st: Over food which, after partaking, one is obligated by Torah law to recite a blessing, one recites a blessing afterward,

chunks.en: but he does not say the bracha before eating.
chunks.st: but one does not recite a blessing beforehand,
chunks.stMore: because the blessing recited prior to eating is a requirement by rabbinic law.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: And in all of these instances Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he says the brachos before them and after them.
chunks.explain: Both for Shema and for food.
chunks.st: He recites a blessing beforehand and thereafter in both the case of Shema and in the case of food.

summary: If a man remembers in the middle of davening that he is tamei, he makes his davening shorter. If he went to the mikvah in the morning, he must cover himself before saying Shema. He may not say Shema in smelly water, and must stay four amos away from a dirty mess.
stIntro: This mishna contains various statements with regard to individuals with different types of ritual impurity as well as the need to distance oneself from filth and impurity.

chunks.en: If a man was standing and davening,
chunks.st: One who was standing in prayer

chunks.en: and he remembered that he is tamei,
chunks.st: and he recalled that he experienced a seminal emission,
chunks.stMore: and according to this opinion he is prohibited from praying,

words.note: A kind of impurity from the body; he must go to the mikvah.

chunks.en: he should not stop,
chunks.st: should not interrupt his prayer,

chunks.en: but he should make each bracha shorter.
chunks.st: rather he should abridge each individual blessing.

chunks.en: If he went down into the mikvah to dip,
chunks.st: They stated a general principle: One who descended to immerse himself,

words.note: To go under the water of a mikvah to become tahor.

chunks.en: if he can come up, get dressed, and say Shema
chunks.st: if he is able to ascend, cover himself with a garment, and recite the morning Shema

chunks.en: before the sun comes up,
chunks.st: before sunrise,

chunks.en: he should come up, get dressed, and say it.
chunks.st: he should ascend, cover himself, and recite Shema,

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if not,

chunks.en: he should cover himself with the water and say it there.
chunks.st: he should cover himself in the water and recite Shema there.

chunks.en: But he should not cover himself
chunks.st: He may not, however, cover himself

chunks.he: לֹא בַמַּיִם הָרָעִים וְלֹא בְמֵי הַמִּשְׁרָה,
chunks.en: not in smelly water and not in water where flax was soaking,
chunks.st: in either foul water, or water in which flax was soaked,

words.note: Water where flax plants were soaked, which smells bad.

chunks.en: until he pours fresh water into it.
chunks.st: until he pours other water into it.

chunks.en: And how far must he stay away from urine and from a dirty mess to say Shema?
chunks.st: And in general, how far must one distance himself from urine and feces in order to recite Shema?
chunks.basisNote: Both explain "them" as urine; Bartenura says some words are missing here.

chunks.en: Four amos.
chunks.st: At least four cubits.

words.note: An amah is about the length of a grown-up's arm, about 2 feet.

summary: Some people who are already tamei in a bigger way also became tamei in a smaller way. The Chachamim say they still need to go to the mikvah before davening and learning, but Rabbi Yehuda says they don't.
stIntro: Continuing the earlier discussion of the halakhot of immersion for Torah study and prayer for one who experienced a seminal emission, the mishna discusses a case where individuals who were already impure with a severe form of ritual impurity are exposed to the impurity of a seminal emission as well. They are required to immerse themselves and purify themselves of the impurity of the seminal emission even though they remain impure due to the more severe impurity.

chunks.en: A zav who also became tamei from a seminal emission,
chunks.st: Consequently, even a zav, whose impurity lasts at least seven days, who experienced a seminal emission,
chunks.stMore: for which, were he not a zav, he would be impure for only one day;

words.note: A man who is tamei for at least seven days because of an illness.
Another kind of impurity from the body.

chunks.en: and a niddah who also became tamei in another way,
chunks.st: a menstruating woman who discharged semen,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that she is already impure with a severe impurity unaffected by her immersion;

words.note: A woman who is tamei for at least seven days at certain times of the month.

chunks.en: and a married woman who became a niddah,
chunks.st: and a woman who engaged in conjugal relations with her husband and later saw menstrual blood,

words.en: and a woman with her husband

chunks.en: all need to go to the mikvah.
chunks.st: all require immersion.

chunks.en: But Rabbi Yehuda says they don't have to.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda exempts them from immersion.

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.
